title: Unify focus-rescue and contrast-fallback for icon-action buttons
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Several regressions surfaced in production where icon-only and compact buttons lose visible focus or provide insufficient contrast in dark/light theme combinations and when token overrides are applied by clients. This causes keyboard users and low-vision users to miss focus state and increases support tickets. Goal: Introduce a predictable 'focus-rescue' and contrast-fallback strategy for icon-action and compact buttons that: 1) automatically raises focus ring contrast when computed contrast is below threshold, 2) expands touch/click hit area for icon-only surfaces without changing visual scale, and 3) integrates an interruptible hold-to-confirm affordance for destructive/dual-action icons so users can cancel mid-gesture.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens introduced: button.icon.focusRingFallback, button.icon.expandedHitbox, button.icon.holdConfirmTimeout and documented in token registry
Icon-only buttons always show a minimum 3:1 focus contrast or fall back to focus-rescue token across themes
Expanded hitbox implemented as logical padding (no layout shift) with visual size unchanged; unit tests cover hit target changes
Hold-to-confirm calls can be canceled within the timeout and show progressive microanimation; keyboard users can cancel via Escape
Design review completed and Figma spec updated; Engineering PR merged with e2e regression tests and telemetry for focus-fallback occurrences
No new accessibility violations in axe/lighthouse and manual A11y QA passes for keyboard and Zoom 200% scenarios
tasks: Audit production incidents and collect examples where focus/contrast failed (Sentry/Support)
Propose token names and fallback algorithm; validate with accessibility consultant
Create Figma components showing default, elevated-fallback, and token-override states across light/dark/high-contrast
Implement CSS token mappings and small runtime helper to compute contrast and toggle fallback
Add unit and visual regression tests (Chromatic + jest-dom) and touch-target integration tests
Ship to canary, monitor telemetry, and roll out with migration notes for clients that override tokens
comments: 2025-11-13 - Aisha Patel: Kicked off audit; pulled Sentry incidents and three support tickets that reference missing focus on icon toolbar in dark theme. Attached screenshots in Confluence.

2025-11-14 - Sofia Gutierrez: Spike completed for fallback algorithm. Proposal: compute contrast between focus ring color token and surface; if < 3.0, swap to button.icon.focusRingFallback or add 2px outer stroke with neutral-contrast token. Need accessibility sign-off.

2025-11-16 - Accessibility (review): Suggested threshold 3.0 for non-text UI controls and confirmed Escape should cancel hold-to-confirm. Also recommended telemetry event 'button.focus_fallback_applied' with boolean and component key.

2025-11-18 - Engineering (Ben Cho): Implemented expandedHitbox as pointer-events padding layer; performance microbenchmark shows negligible layout impact. Pushed initial branch for review at PR #17021.

2025-11-19 - Design QA (Sofia): Updated Figma with interaction specs, added states for token-override and high-contrast mode. Noted an edge case: split-button compound where trailing icon receives focus—added task to handle compound focus order.
2025-11-20 - PM (Marcus Lee): Approved P1 priority and requested release note copy for design-2025.11; asked to include migration guidance for clients with custom tokens.
